deals.headline: MLS awards Cincinnati its 26th team; $150m expansion fee
deals.investor: Carl H. Lindner III and partners
deals.summary: MLS awarded the expansion team to the Lindner-led ownership group on 29 May 2018 (club release, listed in sources), for play from 2019. The $150 million fee is as FOX19 reported it in 2019.

deals.evidence: approximately $200 million in lease revenue bonds and $22 million in Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) bonds
deals.headline: Port Authority to issue about $200m of lease revenue bonds for the West End stadium
deals.investor: Port of Greater Cincinnati Development Authority (bond issuer)
deals.summary: The Port Authority's board approved preliminary terms: the Port issues about $200 million of lease revenue bonds plus $22 million of PACE bonds, owns the stadium and leases it to the team, which carries the assets and liabilities. The amount is the article's approximation of a plan, not a closing figure.

deals.evidence: reportedly purchased a minority 20 percent stake in the soccer club for $100 million
deals.headline: Meg Whitman and Griff Harsh buy into FC Cincinnati
deals.investor: Meg Whitman and Dr. Griff Harsh
deals.summary: The MLS board approved Whitman and Harsh as owners; the Cincinnati Enquirer reported a 20% stake for $100 million, putting the club at $500 million including the stadium, the Milford training ground and the $150 million expansion fee.

deals.evidence: Cincinnati FC had a recent transaction for 4% of the team at a $939 million enterprise value.
deals.headline: 4% of FC Cincinnati changes hands among existing owners at a $939m enterprise value
deals.summary: Sportico reported a recent transaction for 4% of the team at a $939 million enterprise value, the buyers being existing owners; the Cincinnati Business Courier (via WKRC) put the price at a $938 million franchise value. The amount paid is not stated.

founded_evidence: Founded in 2015, FC Cincinnati was born from a bold vision
name: FC Cincinnati
notes: Revenue, operating income and value are Forbes estimates for the 2025 MLS season (Forbes' list of 13 Feb 2026); forbes.com refuses scripted fetches, so the URL cited is the Wayback Machine copy of the same article. Operating income is Forbes' EBITDA-style measure. The commercial figure is Sportico's 'around $30 million' for 2023, from internal MLS documents, shared by Austin, Cincinnati and Columbus; matchday and broadcast are not split out. MLS clubs publish no accounts, so wages, pre-tax result and net debt are blank. Stakes: only the Whitman/Harsh 20% (2019, as reported) is stated; Lindner III's percentage is not published, and the 2025 4% transfer among existing owners may have moved the split. Jeff Berding is President & Co-Chief Executive Officer alongside Lindner III. Attendance and social follower counts were not found on a citable page. In January 2026 the club signed a strategic partnership with FC Porto with no equity stake (Inside World Football); in September 2026 ESPN reported (via Yahoo Sports) that the ownership group had discussed buying NWSL's Racing Louisville FC - not a completed deal.

ownership_summary: Controlled by Carl H. Lindner III, who founded the club with Jeff Berding in 2015; the other managing owners are Meg Whitman and Dr. Griff Harsh (a reported 20% bought for $100m in 2019), Scott Farmer and George Joseph. Lindner III is controlling owner and CEO of both FC Cincinnati Holdings (the wider sporting and development enterprise) and Fussball Club Cincinnati (the team). Existing owners bought a 4% stake in a transaction Sportico reported in January 2025, at a $939m enterprise value. No private-equity, sovereign or other institutional holder is disclosed.
